senses.definition: Having a pleasing appearance, good-looking, attractive, particularly:

quotes.text: Often, human mortals describe their visits to the Tuatha's [places] in similar terms: they were great bright places, occupied by exceedingly handsome men and women, that sported wonderful crystal chairs, inexhaustible supplies of mead or ale ...

subsenses.definition: Of a man or boy: attractively manly, having a pleasing face and overall effect.
examples: I was struck dumb. Here was the most handsome man I’d ever seen in my life coming out of the surf.

quotes.text: Scott was a man then who looked like a boy with a face between handsome and pretty. He had very fair wavy hair, a high forehead, excited and friendly eyes and a delicate long-lipped Irish mouth that, on a girl, would have been the mouth of a beauty. His chin was well built and he had good ears and a handsome, almost beautiful, unmarked nose.
quotes.reference: 1964, Ernest Hemingway, “Scott Fitzgerald”, in A Moveable Feast, New York, N.Y.: Charles Scribner’s Sons, →OCLC, page 149:

subsenses.definition: Of a woman: statuesque, beautiful in a masculine or otherwise imposing way.
examples: She was either handsome or her uniform created a flattering effect but—being very nearsighted—he couldn't tell from this distance.

quotes.text: City have lapped up the plaudits this season for a series of handsome wins but manager Roberto Mancini has demanded that his side also learn to grind out results when they do not play well. He now has an example to point to.

subsenses.definition: (figuratively) Of weather, fine, clear and bright.

quotes.text: Sunday, the sixth, we heaved up our sheet-anchor again, the day beginning with little wind, and continued handsome weather till eight at night, when the wind came to S. S. W. and it fell a snowing.

quotes.text: The story goes that James Whitcomb Riley, the poet, on a beautiful spring day, in making his way from his home to his office, was accosted by numerous friends on the way who were exclaiming most extravagantly on the beauty of the day. It was "Good morning, Mr. Riley, a fine day;" "Good morning, Mr. Riley, […] a handsome day;" […].
